term: abstract, necessary-proposition, absence, totality and external reply content
definition: replyArena uses two universally accessible worlds with a concrete object only at false and a true concrete-negative only at true. An abstractObject exists at both; absence and totalEmpty tokens exist only at true; totalOne has rigid singleton inventory and exists only at false; external exists only at false yet is stipulated to make the negative at true. AbsenceContent equates absence-token eligibility with the negative; TotalityContent exactly matches concrete inventory to rigid empty/singleton content. The separate necessaryArena has no concrete extension anywhere, an always-existing reified-proposition candidate, and necessary negative truth; necessaryMaking is additional, not entailed by truth.
note: These are conditional finite fragments, not historical attributions or complete theories. Nonconcrete is membership outside the supplied concrete extension, not an independent analysis of abstractness. Primitive making is not material implication, efficient causation or an explained grounding mechanism. No transitivity/asymmetry/well-foundedness is assumed. Examples: empty inventory differs from the singleton-object inventory; a true proposition with noMaking is not a maker. The external token is existent elsewhere, unlike outsideMaking which is absent in its control. Counterexamples: necessarily true content cannot by entailment ground this contingent negative; abstract eligibility alone does not supply concrete existence. Generalization to reality, adequate truthmaking relevance, and reification of facts/propositions remain OPEN. Necessary-truth scope differs explicitly from the contingent profile.
